title: 135. Quantitative Relationships & Measurement: Geometric Mean of Positive Values
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Geometric Mean of Two Positive Values
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the geometric mean of two positive numbers.
questions.question: What is the geometric mean of \(4\) and \(9\)?
questions.explanation: The geometric mean of two positive numbers \(a\) and \(b\) is \(\sqrt{ab}\). Here, \(\sqrt{4\times 9}=\sqrt{36}=6\). Therefore, the geometric mean is \(6\). The alternative \(6.5\) is the arithmetic mean, \(\frac{4+9}{2}\).
questions.hint: Look for an equal factor that reproduces the total product.

questions.concept: Geometric Mean of Two Positive Values
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the geometric mean of \(2\) and \(8\).
questions.question: What is the geometric mean of \(2\) and \(8\)?
questions.explanation: The geometric mean of \(2\) and \(8\) is \(\sqrt{2\times 8}=\sqrt{16}=4\). Therefore, the geometric mean is \(4\). The alternative \(5\) is the arithmetic mean, \(\frac{2+8}{2}\).
questions.hint: Distinguish a multiplicative average from an additive average.

questions.concept: Geometric Mean of Three Positive Values
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the geometric mean of three positive numbers.
questions.question: What is the geometric mean of \(1\), \(4\), and \(16\)?
questions.explanation: The product is \(1\times 4\times 16=64\), so the geometric mean is \(\sqrt[3]{64}=4\). The alternative \(7\) is the arithmetic mean, \(\frac{1+4+16}{3}\), rather than the cube root of their product.
questions.hint: Count how many positive factors the geometric mean combines.

questions.concept: Geometric Mean of Two Positive Values
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the geometric mean of \(5\) and \(20\).
questions.question: What is the geometric mean of \(5\) and \(20\)?
questions.explanation: The geometric mean is \(\sqrt{5\times 20}=\sqrt{100}=10\). Therefore, the geometric mean is \(10\). The alternative \(12.5\) is the arithmetic mean, \(\frac{5+20}{2}\).
questions.hint: Look for an equal factor that reproduces the total product.

questions.concept: Finding a Missing Value from a Given Geometric Mean
questions.learningObjective: Determine a missing positive value when the geometric mean is known.
questions.question: The geometric mean of \(2\), \(x\), and \(18\) is \(6\). What is the positive value of \(x\)?
questions.explanation: Cubing the geometric mean gives \(2\times x\times 18=6^3=216\), so \(x=6\). The alternative \(18\) solves \(\sqrt{2x}=6\), omitting the third factor and using a square root instead of a cube root.
questions.hint: Distinguish a multiplicative average from an additive average.

questions.learningObjective: Compare the arithmetic mean and geometric mean for two positive numbers.
questions.question: For the positive numbers \(1\) and \(9\), which statement is true?

options.label: A
options.text: The arithmetic mean is smaller than the geometric mean.

options.label: B
options.text: The geometric mean is smaller than the arithmetic mean.

questions.explanation: The arithmetic mean is \(\frac{1+9}{2}=5\). The geometric mean is \(\sqrt{1\times 9}=3\). Since \(3<5\), the geometric mean is smaller than the arithmetic mean. The opposite inequality is false: the geometric mean is \(3\), whereas the arithmetic mean is \(5\).
questions.hint: Count how many positive factors the geometric mean combines.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the geometric mean annual growth factor from a total growth factor.
questions.question: A quantity grows by a factor of \(9\) over \(2\text{ years}\). What is the geometric mean annual growth factor?
questions.explanation: The geometric mean annual growth factor is the square root of the total growth factor over two years. Here, \(\sqrt{9}=3\). Therefore, the geometric mean annual growth factor is \(3\). The alternative \(4.5\) divides the total factor by the number of years instead of taking its square root.
questions.hint: Look for an equal factor that reproduces the total product.

questions.concept: Geometric Mean of Two Positive Values
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the geometric mean of \(10\) and \(40\).
questions.question: What is the geometric mean of \(10\) and \(40\)?
questions.explanation: The geometric mean is \(\sqrt{10\times 40}=\sqrt{400}=20\). Therefore, the geometric mean is \(20\). The alternative \(25\) is the arithmetic mean, \(\frac{10+40}{2}\).
questions.hint: Distinguish a multiplicative average from an additive average.

questions.concept: Effect of Scaling on the Geometric Mean
questions.learningObjective: Determine the new geometric mean after multiplying every value by a constant.
questions.question: The geometric mean of a set of positive numbers is \(5\). If every number in the set is multiplied by \(4\), what is the new geometric mean?
questions.explanation: Multiplying every value by the same positive constant \(k\) multiplies the geometric mean by \(k\). Here \(k=4\), so the new geometric mean is \(5\times 4=20\). Therefore, the new geometric mean is \(20\). The alternative \(9\) adds the scale factor to the old mean rather than multiplying.
questions.hint: Factor the constant out of the product before taking the root.

questions.concept: Geometric Mean of Successive Growth Factors
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the average annual growth factor using the geometric mean.
questions.question: A quantity increases by a factor of \(3\) in the first year and by a factor of \(12\) in the second year. What is the geometric mean annual growth factor?
questions.explanation: The total growth factor is \(3\times 12=36\). The equivalent annual factor is \(\sqrt{36}=6\). The alternative \(7.5\) uses the arithmetic mean \(\frac{3+12}{2}\), which does not reproduce the same compounded growth.
questions.hint: Look for an equal factor that reproduces the total product.
